From 9478c166c46934160135e197b049b5a05753f2ad Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Nov 2024 11:46:01 +1000
Subject: [PATCH] nouveau/gsp: drop WARN_ON in ACPI probes

These WARN_ONs seem to trigger a lot, and we don't seem to have a
plan to fix them, so just drop them, as they are most likely
harmless.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 176fdcbddfd2 ("drm/nouveau/gsp/r535: add support for booting GSP-RM")
Signed-off-by: Dave Airlie <airlied@redhat.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20241121014601.229391-1-airlied@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Danilo Krummrich <dakr@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c
index 7fb13434c051..a575a8dbf727 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c
@@ -737,8 +737,8 @@ r535_gsp_acpi_caps(acpi_handle handle, CAPS_METHOD_DATA *caps)
 	if (!obj)
 		goto done;
 
-	if (WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) ||
-	    WARN_ON(obj->buffer.length != 4))
+	if (obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER ||
+	    obj->buffer.length != 4)
 		goto done;
 
 	caps->status = 0;
@@ -773,8 +773,8 @@ r535_gsp_acpi_jt(acpi_handle handle, JT_METHOD_DATA *jt)
 	if (!obj)
 		goto done;
 
-	if (WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) ||
-	    WARN_ON(obj->buffer.length != 4))
+	if (obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER ||
+	    obj->buffer.length != 4)
 		goto done;
 
 	jt->status = 0;
@@ -861,8 +861,8 @@ r535_gsp_acpi_dod(acpi_handle handle, DOD_METHOD_DATA *dod)
 
 	_DOD = output.pointer;
 
-	if (WARN_ON(_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE) ||
-	    WARN_ON(_DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList)))
+	if (_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE ||
+	    _DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList))
 		return;
 
 	for (int i = 0; i < _DOD->package.count; i++) {
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

This patch modifies the file `drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/rm/r535/gsp.c` to remove `WARN_ON` macros from several condition checks in three ACPI probe functions. The changes are as follows:

1. **`r535_gsp_acpi_caps`**:  
   - Changed:
     ```c
     if (WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) || WARN_ON(obj->buffer.length != 4))
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     if (obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER || obj->buffer.length != 4)
     ```

2. **`r535_gsp_acpi_jt`**:  
   - Changed:
     ```c
     if (WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) || WARN_ON(obj->buffer.length != 4))
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     if (obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER || obj->buffer.length != 4)
     ```

3. **`r535_gsp_acpi_dod`**:  
   - Changed:
     ```c
     if (WARN_ON(_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE) || WARN_ON(_DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList)))
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     if (_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE || _DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList))
     ```

### Relationship of Modifications

All modifications are in the same file and follow an identical pattern: they replace `WARN_ON` calls (which trigger a kernel warning and then continue) with simple conditional checks that still handle the error case by jumping to a `done` label or returning early. This eliminates the unnecessary kernel warnings, which were frequently triggered and deemed harmless. No logic other than the removal of `WARN_ON` is changed.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
if (WARN_ON(obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER) ||
    WARN_ON(obj->buffer.length != 4))</text>
<text>
if (WARN_ON(_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE) ||
    WARN_ON(_DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList)))</text>
Reason:
These WARN_ON macros trigger kernel warnings whenever the ACPI firmware methods (_CAPS, _JT, _DOD) return data with unexpected types or buffer lengths (e.g., ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER with length ≠ 4, or ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE with count exceeding the expected array size). Such mismatches are benign but cause frequent spurious alerts, as the condition does not indicate a real error—the driver simply skips processing when the condition fails.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
if (obj->type != ACPI_TYPE_BUFFER ||
    obj->buffer.length != 4)</text>
<text>
if (_DOD->type != ACPI_TYPE_PACKAGE ||
    _DOD->package.count > ARRAY_SIZE(dod->acpiIdList))</text>
Reason:
The fix removes the WARN_ON wrappers from the condition checks, converting them to simple if statements. This preserves the intended behavior (skipping the ACPI data processing when the expected format is not met) while eliminating the unnecessary and noisy kernel warnings that were triggered by harmless ACPI responses. The logic remains identical; only the warning is removed.
